clusters.name: Walter's move across the country, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move from Millbrook to Sorrel Valley in March 1952: within months, June's anxiety rose as she wrote daily to her sister left behind, Walter spent long hours away in the trees, Glen fought at his new school, Walter cut off his brother Harlan over their father's land money, June kept to her bed for weeks that winter, the two rowed over money for new trees, and by September June's anxiety eased as she joined the church choir and her letters thinned out. The events cluster in the family's first year away, a shift that opened and then began to settle.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when the late frost took the crop and the bank called in the loan: Walter drank heavily, he and Glen blamed each other, Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank, Carl's asthma worsened that winter, Nora began wetting the bed in April 1969, Ida's heart trouble was found, and by October Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning trees. The events cluster within a year of the loss, a period of strain passing from Walter to Glen and then to the children as the family moved and resettled.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's job loss when the cannery closed in February 1975: Glen was out of work most of that year and sat in the truck for hours, he and Marian fought loudly at night over money, Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night, Nora stopped eating and lost weight that summer, she kept to her room and withdrew from her mother, Walter drank again after six years off it, and by June 1976 Nora was eating again and made the track team. The period opens with Glen's loss and moves through the family as strain between the parents and Nora's response, settling when Glen found work driving for the feed store in March 1976.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into Nora's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma's move from her farm into Nora and Hollis's house in January 1990: Nora and Wilma clashed over the children's bedtimes and meals, Hollis kept out of the rows and took his mother's side, Owen had tantrums at preschool, Wilma took over Lily's care, Nora's eczema flared on both hands, Nora and Hollis rowed most nights, and by summer 1991 when Wilma took a flat in town Nora's eczema cleared. The period runs through a year of household strain, with Nora caught between her husband's alignment with his mother and her own distance from him, until Wilma's move out of the house.

This is an acute episode around a real threat, not a period.

1996–1997: Tess's drinking began in October 1996, Nora's worry and overfunctioning with her sister follow across 1996 and 1997, and Tess stopped drinking in June 1997. One shift that counts sits with Tess's drinking in October 1996 (Nora's anxiety in November), one sits with Tess and Rick's rows in March 1997 (Nora's overfunctioning with Tess marked neverOpens so does not count toward a period), and Tess's functioning improved in June. A recount of shifts that count leaves only Nora's anxiety and the events of Tess's own trouble, so there is not enough in the diagram to choose a reading.
